anchors.description: Overall width between the outer jambs of the two-leaf glazed entrance door of the '64' building, measured horizontally across both leaves at mid height
anchors.visible_evidence: White-framed double glass entrance door at building no. 64; two glazed leaves with centre seam and lever handles, seen nearly frontally under the facade overhang
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Standard double entrance door leaves are 0.735-0.985 m each (DIN 18101), plus frame; slight oblique view of the facade gives about +/-0.2 m

anchors.description: Vertical clear height of one glazed door leaf, from the upper frame line down to the lower frame/threshold line of the '64' entrance
anchors.visible_evidence: Single glazed leaf of the same two-leaf entrance door; the leaf runs from the white head frame to the bottom rail above the concrete threshold
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Door height standards are 2.0-2.4 m for entrance doors; the measured span excludes the top/bottom rails so the leaf height could be 0.05-0.1 m more

anchors.description: Vertical height of the grey double-leaf 'S12 Telefonraum' steel door, from its visible head edge under the canopy down to the threshold above the concrete apron
anchors.visible_evidence: Large grey steel double door labelled 'S12 Telefonraum' with lever hardware and warning labels, set under a protruding concrete canopy on the right facade
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Top edge is partly hidden by the canopy and the bottom edge blends with the concrete apron/threshold; door height standard 2.0-2.4 m plus edge uncertainty

anchors.description: Vertical span between the visible upper and lower right-hand corners of the white A4 notice sheet taped to the grey door
anchors.visible_evidence: White printed notice with a warning triangle, taped with a yellow strip at the top of the grey S12 door; its width-to-height pixel ratio (~0.6-0.7) matches ISO A4 portrait (210 x 297 mm)
anchors.identity_uncertainty: The sheet may be Letter size or slightly curled and the yellow tape may cover the very top edge, shifting the measured span by about 1-2 cm
